title.rendered: Gentleness: The Fruit of the Spirit | Day 8

excerpt.rendered: Ancient Greek horse-trainers used prautēs for a warhorse trained to answer the softest touch of the rein. All the power, fully surrendered to the rider. Gentleness is trained strength.

content.rendered:
Ancient Greek horse-trainers used the word prautēs to describe a warhorse that had learned to answer the softest touch of the rein. All the muscle. All the power. All the speed. Fully surrendered to the rider. That is the Greek word for gentleness in Galatians 5.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, October 1, 2026 | The Fruit of the Spirit, Day 8

Today’s Scripture

“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against such there is no law.”
Galatians 5:22-23 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

Ancient Greek horse-trainers had a specific word for a war horse that had been fully broken to the saddle. The horse was still enormous. Still muscled. Still capable of thundering across a battlefield under a heavily armed rider. But the horse had learned to answer the softest touch of the rein. A gentle pull to the left, the horse turned left. A gentle pull to the right, the horse turned right. All the power was still there. It was now fully surrendered to the rider’s hand. The word for that trained-in responsiveness was prautēs. And when Paul lists the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians 5:23, that is the word he uses for gentleness. The eighth fruit is not weakness. It is trained strength. Power under the control of the Spirit.

This is why the same word can be used both of Moses and of Jesus. Moses, Numbers 12:3 tells us, was “very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.” The same Moses who stood before Pharaoh, called down the plagues, parted the Red Sea, and shaped a nation of two million former slaves. Meekness in the biblical sense has nothing to do with a small personality. It is a fully-powered life whose power has been placed under the hand of God. Jesus uses the same word of Himself in Matthew 11:29. “I am gentle and lowly in heart.” The same Jesus who overturned tables in the Temple and spoke truth to Herod and refused to bow to any earthly authority. Jesus was not weak. He was gentle in the trained-warhorse sense. All the authority, all the power, all the sovereignty of God in Christ, fully surrendered to the will of the Father.

The Passion Translation captures this dimension of the fruit beautifully: “But the fruit produced by the Holy Spirit within you is divine love in all its varied expressions: joy that overflows, peace that subdues, patience that endures, kindness in action, a life full of virtue, faith that prevails, gentleness of heart, and strength of spirit” (Galatians 5:22-23 TPT). Gentleness of heart. The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “But the fruit of the (Holy) Spirit [the work which His presence within accomplishes] is love, joy (gladness), peace, patience (an even temper, forbearance), kindness, goodness (benevolence), faithfulness, gentleness (meekness, humility)” (Galatians 5:22-23 AMPC). Meekness. Humility. Both are ways of naming the same thing. Strength that has learned to submit.

The world often mistakes gentleness for softness. It is not. A gentle person can be firm. A gentle person can speak the truth. A gentle person can lead a company, raise a strong-willed child, stand up to injustice, hold a difficult conversation, or make an unpopular decision. But they will do all of it without the harshness the flesh often adds. They will handle the strong things with the softness Jesus modelled with the woman at the well, with the disciples at the foot-washing, with Peter after the denial. Strength is present. Harshness is not. That is the fruit the Holy Spirit is producing.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the fruit the Spirit is growing in you. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, do not confuse gentleness with weakness. The Spirit is not making you a doormat. He is making you a warhorse that answers the softest touch of the rein. All the strength you have been given, fully surrendered to the hand of the King. Let Him ride. Let Him direct. The gentleness the world sees in you is the fruit of a strength that has been submitted to the Rider.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that gentleness is a fruit of Your Spirit in my life. Not weakness. Trained strength. All the power You have given me, fully surrendered to the touch of Your hand. Today I hand You the reins. Whatever You direct me to, I turn toward. Whatever You direct me from, I turn from. And in every relationship and every situation, I ask You to remove the harshness the flesh adds and produce in me the gentleness Jesus modelled. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Gentleness is the fruit of the Spirit in my life today. My strength is surrendered to the Master’s hand. I am a warhorse trained to answer the softest touch of the rein. Powerful, and gentle at the same time.
